name: A Buenos Aires patio

place_source.title: Wikidata: Buenos Aires (Q1486), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A walled courtyard behind a two-storey Buenos Aires house: paved, with a strip of earth along the wall, a naranjo and a peach in the corner, a privet clipped flat against the street side, a maguey by the step. Pairs of horneros work an old clay oven on the wall, chingolos work the open ground, big picazuro pigeons come down from the trees, and after dark a zarigüeya noses along the bins.

facts.text: Under the Köppen climate classification, Buenos Aires has a humid subtropical climate (Cfa).

source.title: Wikipedia: Buenos Aires
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Buenos Aires", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: As a result of maritime influences from the adjoining Atlantic Ocean, the climate is temperate with extreme temperatures being rare; summers are hot and humid and winters are rather cool with mild temperatures during the day and chilly nights.

source.title: Wikipedia: Buenos Aires
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Buenos Aires", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The city lies in the pampa region and has over 250 parks and green spaces, the largest concentration of them on the eastern side in the neighborhoods of Puerto Madero, Recoleta, Palermo and Belgrano.

source.title: Wikipedia: Buenos Aires
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Buenos Aires", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The rufous hornero is a medium-sized ovenbird that occurs in eastern South America and is the national bird of Argentina; it is synanthropic and builds a large thick clay oven on a tree, or on man-made structures such as fence posts, telephone poles or buildings.

source.title: Wikipedia: Rufous hornero
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Rufous hornero", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: In its native range the monk parakeet is very common, and its population explosion in South American rural areas seems to be associated with the expansion of eucalyptus forestry, which offers the bird the opportunity to build protected nests.

source.title: Wikipedia: Monk parakeet
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Monk parakeet", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The rufous-collared sparrow can be seen in virtually any open or semi-open habitat, including cultivations, gardens, parks, grasslands and scrubby second growth, and it copes well with urban and suburban environments.

source.title: Wikipedia: Rufous-collared sparrow

facts.text: Argentine black and white tegus are native to Argentina as well as to Brazil, Paraguay and Bolivia, and significant populations occur in the southern United States from released pet-trade animals; in the wild they try to run away or react aggressively if provoked.

source.title: Wikipedia: Argentine black and white tegu
